extracted.intended_audience: researchers, policy-makers, and funding-agency staff interested in gender bias in grant peer review
extracted.subtask_short: meta-analysis of gender bias in grants
extracted.subtask_description: A meta-analysis synthesizing empirical studies of gender differences in grant peer review across multiple countries and funding agencies, testing moderators and providing implications for rubric and process design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome variable: probability of grant award (effect size)
rubrics_metrics.description: Probability of grant award given application; effect size = log odds ratio of male vs. female success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use log odds ratios (or converted standardized effect sizes) to quantify gender differences in award probability; report pooled effect and confidence intervals. Be explicit about the outcome definition (award/no award) and unit of analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pooled effect size / magnitude
rubrics_metrics.description: Pooled effect: men had ~7% greater odds of grant success than women; effect size: d = 0.04 (small but statistically significant).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report both practical (percent odds) and standardized effect-size metrics; interpret small pooled effects in light of potential large effects in particular contexts and the possibility of heterogeneity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heterogeneity across studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Substantial heterogeneity across studies — some show clear bias, some show none.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess and report heterogeneity (e.g., I^2, between-study variance); investigate moderator variables rather than assuming a uniform effect; interpret pooled estimates cautiously when heterogeneity is large.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding type as moderator
rubrics_metrics.description: Funding type — research grants vs fellowships vs scholarships; effect was larger for fellowships than for project grants in some cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate application categories when analyzing bias; expect stronger investigator-focused bias in fellowships/scholarships and weaker bias in project-focused grants; avoid aggregating heterogeneous funding types without moderation analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Country / system differences
rubrics_metrics.description: Country / system — effects vary by country and funding system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include country/system as a moderator; consider institutional policies and historical contexts (e.g., earlier systems with less formalized criteria may show larger bias).

rubrics_metrics.name: Field/discipline as moderator
rubrics_metrics.description: Field — life sciences, physical sciences, social sciences, humanities; field effects were inconsistent — no single field uniformly worse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze discipline-specific patterns but avoid overgeneralizing; recognize inconsistent field-level effects and examine field-specific review practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Career stage as moderator
rubrics_metrics.description: Career stage — junior vs senior applicants; bias may differ by career stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stratify analyses by applicant career stage; fellowships/junior awards may show different gender patterns than senior project grants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Year of study / temporal trend
rubrics_metrics.description: Year of study — effect was larger in older studies; newer agencies may have reduced bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test for time trends and cohort effects; evaluate whether reforms and changing norms correlate with reduced gender differences over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant pool size
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant pool size was studied as a potential moderator of gender effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include applicant pool characteristics (size, composition) when modeling success probabilities, as selection dynamics may influence observed gender disparities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer access to applicant identity / anonymization
rubrics_metrics.description: Effect was larger when reviewers had access to applicant identity vs anonymized review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement anonymized review (where feasible) to reduce measured gender bias; when evaluating processes, compare outcomes under identified vs anonymized conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator-quality criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigator-quality criterion — perceptions of competence/promise appear to be a pathway for gender bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that emphasis on perceived investigator quality (promise, reputation) creates opportunities for subjective bias; operationalize investigator assessment or shift emphasis to proposal/science to mitigate bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: CV evaluation practices
rubrics_metrics.description: CV evaluation — identical CVs are read differently for women; unstructured CV evaluation contributes to gender gaps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid unstructured CV/track-record assessments; use standardized, operationalized metrics or blinded indicators where appropriate; explicitly adjust CV-based criteria for career interruptions and systemic disparities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters-of-recommendation language
rubrics_metrics.description: Letter-of-recommendation language — gendered descriptors in letters can influence reviewer perceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of and, if possible, standardize or limit the influence of recommendation letter language; provide guidance to letter writers and train reviewers to recognize gendered language effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Productivity expectations / raw publication counts
rubrics_metrics.description: Productivity expectations — reliance on 'raw' publication counts may favor men due to baseline disparities (career interruptions, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjust productivity metrics for career stage, parental leave, part-time work, and structural differences; prefer context-aware indicators over raw counts when assessing past productivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rubric design implication: emphasize science over investigator
rubrics_metrics.description: Rubrics that emphasize the investigator (CV, letters) generate larger gender gaps than those emphasizing the science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design review rubrics to prioritize the quality and feasibility of the proposed science/approach rather than subjective assessments of the applicant; operationalize criteria for evaluating the proposal itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operationalize criteria and de-emphasize unstructured assessments
rubrics_metrics.description: Reform suggestion: de-emphasize unstructured CV evaluation in favor of operationalized criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create clear, structured scoring rubrics with specific evidence requirements; provide explicit scoring anchors and reduce open-ended judgment prompts that invite bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audit historical decisions for gender effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Reform suggestion: audit historical decisions for gender effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regularly analyze past funding decisions by gender (and intersectional characteristics) to detect systematic disparities and evaluate the impact of policy changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track effects of reform efforts longitudinally
rubrics_metrics.description: Reform suggestion: track effects of reform efforts longitudinally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor outcomes over time after implementing process changes (e.g., anonymization, rubric changes) to assess whether reforms reduce gender disparities; report results transparently.
